record.question: Which of the following drug is not used for infective diarrhoea?
record.explanation: Answer C: Miconazole. Miconazole is an antifungal drug, not an antibacterial treatment for infective diarrhea. Source/context note: Most acute infectious diarrhea is managed with rehydration; antibiotics are used selectively. Reference: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=miconazole. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
